utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Naletilic, how are you feeling today? We are quite worried about your health.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my therapy has been increased and I believe that I will be able to cope. It would be really good if I had a break to recuperate after the surgery. If that would be possible, maybe next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you have any requests, would you please inform your counsel and ask your counsel to inform us about any requests for your recovery?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I would just like to inform you that we have already filed a request, I don't know whether it has reached you already, and I believe that we have already received the reply from our colleagues. We believe that as far as the request is concerned, it would be much more logical to give us a break so that my client could rest from a very tiresome sitting in the courtroom day in, day out, so it would be better that we had this break now or instead of God forbid something even worse happened and then this break could be even longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we have received two motions filed by you today. One is about the recess for about two weeks. Another is about another matter. And as for the decisions, I believe that any decisions made by this Trial Chamber will be based on the medical reports from the doctors. Now we are waiting for the report filed by the doctors. If we have that report, I believe that this Trial Chamber will be in a position to make the decisions. Shall we go to the private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. As for your next witness, I think this Trial Chamber is seized with a motion asking for longer time for direct examination, and the -- I hope you could understand that we are already behind schedule and we have heard about 11 background witnesses already. So in this case, this Trial Chamber will give you one hour and 30 minutes for your direct examination for the next witness, so that we could finish with this witness today. It is so decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours. I believe that we will finish today, but I would like to inform you why such situations occur, because, Your Honours, I did not have the time to -- I didn't have five years to prepare myself but sometimes witnesses will tell me things that they haven't told me before or they bring me documents that I then deem very important and I deem that I should inform Your Honours about it. Now I have a lot of experience in direct examination and I now can tell that I usually spend as long as ten minutes just to ask about the general background information. So I did not have any experience before and I didn't know how much direct examination can take and I thank you for your understanding and for understanding our problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We want -- we would like to have distortion of the face and a nickname, because this gentleman, this witness, lives in one location and he intends to return to the town where he used to live, and his knowledge about these events and about these places and the fact that he has witnessed thereof could create a lot of problems for him, but maybe he would be able to explain that much better than I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I guess there is no objections on that issue. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. We don't have any objections but actually it's the first time we hear that this witness needs protective measures. So during the break, we will make some arrangements to make changes in our list of witnesses -- exhibits to be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. used during the cross to remove the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. The Prosecutor is right. It was our agreement that on the day of the trial, we actually have to inform everybody about the minor measures of protection. Only when we want a closed session that this should be asked in advance in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your understanding. So your request for the protective measures is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, to show respect to my colleague in the Prosecution, we -- this week, we are going to ask for all our witnesses, the same type of protective measures so that distortion of their faces and pseudonyms, and that is all. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, could we have the witness, please? [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, you may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, your time begins to run.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me just give you some general instructions that I give to all my witnesses. First of all, I kindly ask you for your cooperation, since we are speaking the same language, to -- in order to enable our interpreters to do their job as best as they can, I'm kindly asking you to look at the screen in front of you and you will see the cursor that is moving, the black point that is moving. When it stops, only then you start giving your answer and try to find a middle speed when you are giving your answers so that we can go through your testimony as fast as we can. Now, the usher is going to show you on the piece of paper, there is your name, but don't say the name, just say yes if that indeed is your name on the piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We are going to call you Witness NE here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask Your Honours to go to the private session so that the witness can give us information about himself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, just let me explain when we ask for the private session, that means that what you're saying can only be heard in this courtroom, whereas during an open session it can be heard also in the gallery, so make sure that you do not reveal your identity in your replies. So do not -- do not -- make sure you don't spontaneously reveal your identity if you do want to do so we will go back to the private session. You can start answering my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: So you asked me to tell you something about Jablanica. Jablanica is in the northern part of Herzegovina, some 45 kilometres north of Mostar. It is a small community, small municipality, 289 square kilometres in size, according to the 1991 census, Jablanica had about 12.500 inhabitants, of whom 2.990 were Croats, who accounted for 18 per cent. 7.000 Muslims who accounted for -- excuse me, 9.000 Muslims who accounted for 70 per cent. About 500 Serbs, who accounted for 4.5 per cent. Yugoslavs accounted for 4.5 per cent also. And there were about 200 people of other -- who did not opt for any specific national affiliation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did this population structure change in 1992 or 1993? Or perhaps we should move towards the beginning of the war in Bosnia in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: My state is called Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the ethnic structure in Jablanica changed when the war started, when the aggression started, against Bosnia and Herzegovina. Since, in the Jablanica municipality, there were no armed operations of the Yugoslav People's Army, that is there were no conflicts, which did break out in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, notably East Bosnia, and since that was the case, a large number of refugees from East Bosnia found shelter in Jablanica. In late 1992, the number of refugees from East Bosnia and East Herzegovina too, totalled about 10.000, and in early 1993, that number rose to some 15.000. So the number of refugees exceeded the number of the domiciled population. And the answer therefore is that the ethnic structure in the municipality of Jablanica in 1992 and 1993 significantly changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If you know, how many Croats and Serbs are there now? What was their influx?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Well, in Jablanica now, one does not have 80 per cent of Croats and 5 per cent of Serbs. Now Croats account for less than 8 per cent and Serbs less than 1 per cent. As -- of the total population which is the municipality of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us, if you know, you say that there were no -- there were no -- there was no fighting in Jablanica with the JNA or rather the Army of Republika Srpska. So where were the first front lines facing the JNA, that is the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right, in the municipality of Jablanica, there were -- there was no open fighting, but if I may be more precise, there were a couple of cases when the aircraft of the Yugoslav air force flew over the area and threw bombs. Fortunately, there were no human casualties or any material damage in the Jablanica municipality. And as for the front lines facing the Serb forces, in the territory of the municipality of Jablanica, there were none. These front lines were in the neighbourhood municipality, the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the citizens of the municipality of Jablanica or the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did they man those front lines in Konjic? Do you know something about how the military structure was organised in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Well, although I wasn't a soldier, because of my poor health, I was more or less familiar with the military organisation of those forces, and I know that in the territory of Jablanica, there was the 44th Mountain Brigade of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there were two more or two autonomous battalions too, in Sovici and Glogosnica. These are the largest in the Jablanica municipality. As regards the Croat Defence Council, it had one battalion, some 60 to 80 men strong and a military police platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In 1992, did they go to the front line facing the Serb forces together? And where is it that they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. I know that in 1992, members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and members of the Croat Defence Council from Jablanica, on a number of instances, went into the territory of the Konjic municipality to man those defence lines against the Serb forces, and that was in the municipality of Konjic, in the area towards Boracko Jezero Lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If you know something about that, we heard some testimony that the front lines facing the Serbs were manned in the area of Sovici or rather in the hills above Sovici, so-called Pasije Stijene toward Blidinje, towards Rama Valley. Are you aware of that? You said that the front lines toward the Serbs were there. Are you aware of the front lines there, that is in Sovici, the hills above Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I know that in the hills above Sovici, that is in the area of Pasije Stijene and Borovnik and those areas, members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Sovici Battalion, that they manned positions there but those positions were not facing Serb forces because I've already told you that in the Jablanica municipality, there were absolutely no Serb forces or Serb front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. So this is 1992. We'll move to 1993 later on. Will you now be so kind as to tell us whether schools worked and how were -- how was the government organised? How was the administration organised in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: First question, schools did not work, neither the elementary nor the secondary, not even the nursery, because these facilities were used to accommodate Muslim refugees from East Bosnia, and as for the local government in Jablanica, no sooner was the state of war proclaimed than the wartime presidency came into being and started to function as the executive branch of power under wartime circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I want to go through this very quickly. This is merely for the Honourable Court. So can you tell me very briefly who won the elections in Jablanica and what was the composition of the executive body of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: On the basis of the election results in the end -- towards the end of 1991, in the -- no, excuse me, 1990, in the very early days of 1991, a body of representatives was constituted and the executive and the government in Jablanica were constituted. The victorious parties were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, why don't you put your head set like I am doing? Otherwise, you'll keep losing it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Right. So the parties which won the elections were the Party of Democratic Action, the Croat Democratic Union, SDP, Social Democratic Party, liberals, reformists, and I don't know, perhaps there were one or two small parties. On the basis of those results, the body of representatives, that is the municipal hall, the municipal council, had nine Croat councilmen, of whom two came from SDP and seven from the HDZ. I know that two councilmen were of Serb origin and the others came from amongst the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now the executive power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The executive power, that was made up exclusively of Muslims and Croats and the ratio was as follows. The government had seven members, of whom five came from amongst the ranks of the Muslim people and two from amongst the ranks of the Croat people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, what were the reactions, of course, if you know of them, when the HZ HB, that is Croat Community Herceg-Bosna was established, the reactions in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The reaction to the establishment of the HZ HB in the municipality of Jablanica was favourable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the HZ HB accepted? Were there allies? Did they take part in the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: There were allies but they did not take a direct part in the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us, what language was spoken in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my mistake. You're quite right. Perhaps I'm not being clear enough. What was the official language in school, in the municipal authorities? What language was spoken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I said that in 1992, schools were closed, and the municipal authorities, we, the Croats, spoke Croatian, and the representatives of the Muslim people spoke their language. And the Serbs spoke, once again, their language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell us, what about work? What about jobs? Did a company go on working? Who lost jobs, if anyone, that is lost jobs? What do you know about that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Because movement of both people and goods was restricted, many companies in Jablanica reduced their business activities and some closed down altogether. Therefore, many people were placed on so-called "waiting lists," sent home, and my wife was also laid off or rather put on a waiting list, even though she used to work for a company which continued working at its former capacity. She worked for the hydro power plant which of course continued working but she was sent home, and I refused to believe at the time that she had been laid off for political reasons. I thought there were some objective reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you all this because, according to the indictment, it is said that the Croats in the municipality of Jablanica engaged in ethnic discrimination, persecution of Muslims, that they imposed a Croatian language. That is why I asked you all this. What can you tell me about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Distinguished sir, if you listened carefully to the demographic facts that I presented to you and the ethnic composition, then it is quite impossible, quite impossible, for the Croats to do what you say they did. That is, they could not engage in ethnic persecution. They could not impose anything. They simply could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, now we've come to the War Presidency, what about the regular authorities? Did they continue to work? We are moving towards 1993 gradually now. What about the legal -- the lawful authorities? Did they continue in operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I have already said the loyal authorities continued to work in so far as the objective circumstances and condition in Jablanica permitted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about the War Presidency? When was it instituted and when did it start its work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The War Presidency came into life sometime in April, 1992, and as we -- as the end of 1992 drew closer, the conditions for the work of the War Presidency grew ever more complicated and its work became harder by the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you ever personally meet with the Muslim leaders, either military or civilian, Mr. Delalic, for instance? Did you know him, did you ever meet him at that time, late 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I was a member of the War Presidency in the municipality of Jablanica, from April, 1992, until October that same year. And during that time, I had opportunity on a number of occasions to see Mr. Delalic, and I personally had the opportunity on the 31st of August, 1992, to attend an official meeting chaired by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what is Mr. Delalic? Will you tell the Court why we mention his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic, in Jablanica and Konjic, was known as a businessman. However, in 1992, when he turned up as the commander of the Technical Group 1, in the territory between the Igman Mount to -- and Konjic and Jablanica, with very broad powers, he caused some perplexity and that goes for both the Army of BH and the local military authorities. I mean, even they could not understand who gave him his powers and how did he come to hold that post. But as the time went by, they grasped the situation and stopped being surprised by his powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And why did he cause this perplexity even amongst the ranks of the Army of BH? I mean what was his mission? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Well, it was because, in the first place, concerning the appointment or designation of the commander, rather the local commander, of the BH Army, because he was the one who appointed him, at the time, when the procedure was completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. But did he cause some incidents? Did the relations, between the BH Army and this very small HVO, change after his arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. But let us go back to that meeting of the 31st of August, 1992. The meeting was convened at the initiative of both parties, that is the BH Army and the HVO, in the municipalities of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, in order to discuss and reach an agreement on the future joint struggle against the Serb forces, that is the JNA, and the Serb armed forces. And as the meeting took place in Jablanica, we were expecting that the meeting would be chaired by the president of the War Presidency of the municipality of Jablanica, that is a kind of a custom with us, that is the host, Mr. Nijaz Ivkovic, that he would be the host, that is the chairman of the meeting. However, when Mr. Delalic entered the room where the meeting was to take place, he, in a rather arrogant manner, took the chair and started to conduct the meeting, which took everybody present by surprise, and as for the contents, those present were further perplexed and confused, and when I say that I mean the members of the HVO and the BH Army when Mr. Delalic insisted most emphatically that the HVO in the territory of Konjic, Prozor and Jablanica be unconditionally subordinated -- I mean command to be subordinated to the command of the BH Army, and he said roughly like this, that the HVO had to do it or else it would be no more in those areas, in that territory. That meeting largely brought about the loss of confidence between the BH Army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did he also settle physically the scores with Muslims who refused to obey him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. And I'll quote a bad -- a bad example. A month after the meeting that I've just mentioned, Mr. Delalic ordered, commanded, the local commander of the military police to bring in, to put in custody, Mr. Ivkovic, the president of the War Presidency in Jablanica, to put him under custody in the museum in Jablanica, and it was done. And when, after he was taken in, Mr. Delalic, slapped him in the face twice. Mr. Ivkovic informed us about this at the meeting, at the session of the War Presidency, the next day. And apart from this, there were a number of other incidents and truth to tell, people tried -- shunned Mr. Delalic because he earned a reputation as an arrogant man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who did the civilian authority rely on? Where was the administrative seat of Jablanica municipality? Was it Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I already spoke about the organisation of the local government; in -- during the war. However, some sectors, some segments, of this local government, local authorities, were tied to their respective regions. For example, in Mostar, the local police, that was the public security station, was linked or tied with the intermunicipal or regional MUP, the Ministry of the Interior in Mostar, and they had the obligation to receive their instructions from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question: Did that relationship change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: This relationship did change. Already in the second half of 1992, the local MUP, that's the local police, stopped communicating with Mostar, although they were under the obligation to do so, but they were instructed to communicate with Zenica. This is an entirely different region, because we -- there are -- there is Sarajevo between the two of us, so it is a totally illogical situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My time is very limit so I want to move quickly to a certain event. I just wanted to provide Their Honours with the general information. Let's go to 1991. What is the relationship between the Muslims and Croats and what happened in 1993? So we are moving on to that conflict in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In 1993, I was no longer a member of the local War Presidency. I was also sent home to wait, so to say, so I stopped working in the municipality. I was put on a waiting list. And the relationship between the local Muslim and the local Croatian population were no longer as they used to be in 1992 for the reasons that I have already spoken about, and also for the fact that in the town itself and in the entire municipality, there was a large number of Muslim refugees. So this resulted in minor incidents. This resulted in a small-scale looting of Croatian property. So the number of car thefts increased, a large number of shops were broken into and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I am a bit panicky, I have another 40 minutes left and I have two major subjects to cover. We have lost quite a lot of time in the introduction. Can you say to the Honourable Court when did things change radically in Jablanica and Prozor municipalities, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. My wish is to say exactly that to the Honourable Court here. The relationship changed radically for the worst, that is the relationship between the Croatian and Muslim population in Jablanica, by the arrival of Mr. Safet Cibo and his appointment as the president of the War Presidencies of Jablanica, Konjic and Prozor municipalities. His arrival was actually a major precedent, both in legal and political terms. Actually, he was a person from Sarajevo. He did not take part in the election in 1991. And he could not be the president of these municipalities. This was another cause for confusion. He arrived pursuant to an act, a document, which was signed by the then president of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Immediately upon his arrival, and that was the beginning of March, 1993, the local television aired his reasons for his arrival. He spoke on the local television about that, and he outlined briefly the programme for his activities. He established a national, nationally-based War Presidency, ethnically based War Presidency, which -- in which there were no longer Croats. So it was a monoethnic Presidency and at the same time, on parallel with his arrival in the area of Jablanica municipality, also saw an arrival of a large number of armed, unknown soldiers. Later on we found out that those were the following units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Those were the special detachment for special purposes, at the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Then the Black Swans. Then the so-called "Walter's Unit," and the commander of that was a person known as "Silver Fox." Then the Wolves from Igman. Cedo's, Celo's, the Handzar Division. Since these people were armed, they started causing more serious incidents. They actually expelled the HVO and the military police of the HVO from Jablanica. And they also took a number of repressive measures. Actually, we realised that their primary -- the primary goal of Mr. Safet Cibo was to make the lives of us Croats in Jablanica as difficult as possible. The measures that he introduced ranged from the mild ones, like, for example, our phone lines were cut off so all of us lost telephone connections. People, all of us, were laid off in the companies where they had worked. People were sent to become members of the so-called "task forces" or work units. They were forced to do manual labour regardless of their age, regardless of their level of education, regardless of their health conditions. So all the Croats had to engage in forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which month are you referring to in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the end of March and the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did armed conflicts also start in the area of Jablanica, Konjic, Prozor, between the HVO and the Army of BH? Who was attacking whom? What about the civilian population of these three municipalities, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: According to a previously prepared scenario -- actually according to a document which was signed by the commanders of several brigades of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army, and chiefs of police stations in Jablanica, Konjic, Hadzici, so according, pursuant to this document, the contents of which are terrible --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to show this document. I'm just waiting for you to finish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Shall I give you a brief answer? So the incidents started on 25th of March. There was the -- there were the first killings without any reason whatsoever of several aged civilians in Orliste, that is a village in the general area of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was the nationality of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: They were Croats. They were elderly Croatian civilians. And later on, this repeated in several other villages in Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can I ask Madam Registrar to put the Exhibit 1336 -- D1336? Since the Court has given me an hour and a half for the examination, I wanted to show all the documents that you brought with you at the end of the examination together with your short comments. I would like to show the Honourable Court all these documents, because I deem that the Honourable Court will find these documents very important. So we would like to listen to your live testimony on all of these topics that we have mentioned. When you were talking about the document, did you mean the document that you now have in front of you? Is that the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely the document that I referred to. If you look at this document closely --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you give us the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The date is 20 March, 1993. On page 2 of this document, you can see that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the police of the aforementioned municipalities, wanted in a forcible way, I'm referring to item 2, in a forcible way, they wanted to take over the control of the checkpoints and passages. They wanted to do that unilaterally. And some of them are mentioned here in. Out of these three are in the area of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document, it says that the HVO was to blame for all this. Can you look at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the beginning of this page very well. However this is just a deception. Don't trust this. This is a deception, this is just an excuse, a very cunning excuse, for the military and armed operations that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was planning to undertake. Please, on page 3 of the same document, under item 7, they are using the following terminology: The HVO all of a sudden is the aggressor. And the BH Army concentrates its troops on the -- in the direction of Jablanica, Pute, Here, Scipe. There were never any Serb forces here. There were none here at the time. So I -- we wonder. This makes us wonder what was the goal of the BH Army, and the goal was to eliminate the HVO from this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Item 9, army forces are to be prepared for taking Slater facility as soon as possible. What is the Zlatar facility or feature? What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Zlatar is a point, a feature, in Konjic municipality, which was held by HVO members in Konjic, but actually, this was a front line facing the Serb forces. The BH Army wanted to expel the HVO, and they managed in doing that, from this feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, according to your knowledge, very briefly, the fate of Croats, or the intensity of conflicts, can you tell us about the fate of Konjic, the area of Konjic, until 15 of April? Not after the 15th of April. So what happened in Konjic before the 15th of April, and the valley, the Neretva Valley, towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Pursuant to this plan, this scenario, contained in this document, already five days after the date on the document, the first Croatian civilian victims fell in Orliste that is a village in the general area of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's move to Konjic, the town of Konjic, and then we shall move down the valley?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In the town of Konjic, the situation was similar as in Jablanica. The HVO was pushed out forcibly from the town --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe the witness will specify the source of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now that you were talking about Konjic, what is the source of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I personally saw some people, my acquaintances, from Konjic, who were expelled. And I have broader knowledge of this from documents, from a number of documents, in the Commission for War Crimes after I left the camp in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, it is very important when you talk about some knowledge, can you please tell us whether the knowledge is personal or whether you learned about that from somebody else. Then give us the names. In the indictment, it says that on 16 April, the HVO forces attacked undefended Muslim civilians and this is how the persecution of Muslims started in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's why I asked you what happened before the 15th of April in the territory of your municipality. So can you please give the Honourable Court the fate of the civilians and the army in the -- in your municipality before the 15th of April? If you don't have any personal knowledge, tell us, "I was told by my brother, by my friend, by my acquaintance." Just give us their names and the Honourable Court will accept that as your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The town of Konjic, as for the town of Konjic, I have personal knowledge about the period -- relative period. This personal knowledge is based on my contacts with my acquaintances from Konjic. Those are Professor Mirko Loncar, and Mr. Marijan Mendes, whom I know even better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what happened, just a brief outline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The HVO was expelled from Konjic. The first armed provocations started in the town. I've already mentioned the incidents in some villages. In the town, the HVO members who were taken prisoner in Zlatar and in other places, the camp "Musala" was organised in the facility sports hall in the town. Later on, this facility would house approximately 900 detained HVO members. And those Croats who were not detained in the camp, they were engaged in forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about the religious officials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The religious officials?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Quite gradually we are going down to tu quoque defence. And that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are not interested in this matter, whether the HVO members were detained or mistreated. It's not a subject of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not bring this witness to tu quoque defence. I am here attacking the indictment, which alleges that the HVO was the force that started a widespread attack on civilians, civilian Muslim population, and started an ethnic persecution. Your Honours, have to hear the witness -- the testimony from the witnesses who were there, and you have to hear what really happened, because this allegation in the indictment is just not true, and as the Defence counsel, I have the right to communicate the truth to this Honourable Court. I'm not defending my case tu quoque. So this -- if Your Honours just hear the date when the HVO members were detained, and what was the destiny of the civilians, we are talking about a region which is about several hundred kilometres large so I wanted to -- this witness to tell you what happened before the 15th of April, 1993. What was the destiny of the civilians? What was the personal destiny of this witness? You are going to hear from him what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we understand that during the war, terrible things were committed both parties. There is no doubt about that. But that is not a subject matter of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can please the Persecution withdraw their allegation from the indictment alleging that the HVO started the persecution of Muslims. And then I will withdraw my witnesses who will -- and I will stop trying to prove that this is not true. The Army of BH started this persecution, and the attack on HVO in the late 1992, and this lasted throughout 1993, continuously. So it does make the difference who attacked whom first and why. And the crimes in this area, that's another issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it seems to me that we are talking about different things. You could claim that the HVO did not commit any crimes against the Muslims and there is no doubt at all that the Muslims also committed some terrible crimes against HVO. There is no problem about that. But the issue is -- but the issue is here, it's about whether there is widespread persecution committed by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not alleging that the HVO or members of the HVO did not commit any crimes or the BH Army. What I am alleging -- what I am saying, and I'll prove that through my witnesses, that the BH Army was the one that attacked both the civilian Croatian population and the HVO and in order for me to prove this, you have to hear my witness, because I'm referring to the dates prior to the 15th of April, and that's why I always said that on the 9th of May -- May, Mostar did not fall out of the blue sky, that this is based on a long history and in order for to us prove that, we have to hear this testimony. I'm not -- I'm not trying to defend a crime by another crime. That would not be a serious defence. But the allegation contained in the indictment asked for this kind of defence, and asked for a proper, truthful reply. Because it is just not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the jurisprudence of this Tribunal is not to find the truth of the whole situation. Here, we are Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. only going to address those issues mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Your Honours, in the indictment, it says that in Jablanica, the HVO persecuted -- persecuted Muslims and engaged in ethnic cleansing. This is what it says in the indictment. It says in the indictment that my client participated in the widespread attack that started on 16th of April, and that he himself personally was engaged in this persecution. This is a close link. And please, would the Prosecution give up all the allegations in the indictment which refer to the widespread conflict? And would we kindly -- I'm kindly asking you to just concentrate on individual crimes. Let's just concentrate on individual crimes. How come -- why is the indictment construed in this way? I have to attack all of its parts. Can please the Prosecution give up on this general part? Let's just focus on what Mr. Naletilic did. And let's just focus on the things that the lawyers do. I'm challenging the Prosecution to give us the evidence for the general allegations in the indictment. In this general context, they have pinpointed my client. That is why I have to attack every item, every count, in the indictment, and I have to attack that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it seems to me that we are talking along different lines. The issue here is whether the HVO committed some crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't want to speak about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you claim that that they did not commit any crimes, you can show some evidence on that. The issue is not what committed by the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, far be it from me to say that some HVO members or the HVO did not commit crimes. All I want to say here is that they were the ones -- they were not the ones who started the attack, who attacked first the Muslim population, as the indictment says, and that is why I brought witnesses so that you could hear about. This is a very large area where hundreds of thousands of people lived and I bring them here for -- so that you can hear what happened before the 15th of April. This is quite clear. I'm only referring to what the indictment says. And if the indictment says that Jablanica was ethnically cleansed by Croats, then why don't you hear from a man who lived there for 35 years to tell us whether that is true or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, since we are under the very strict time pressure, could we have our break here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I hope during the break, you could discuss this matter with your co-counsel and your team on that very issue. Yes. We will resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, could we have the witness, please? Mr. Krsnik, you have about 20 minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the -- my learned friends do not object, I really won't be able to do it in 20 minutes because we have to go through these documents. Of course we won't be reading them because they speak for themselves and I have another subject to cover, which is what this witness knows about Sovici and Doljani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, try your best, and on the other hand, I believe that those documents speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours, but there are quite a number of them. I've got ten documents. Of course, we will not be reading them because they are self-evident, but I need their provenance confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit down, Witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you one question and I will ask for a brief answer, please. And then we shall go through documents very quickly because all I need is the source of these documents, that is how I came by them. And then we shall round off with your information about Jablanica, or rather about Sovici and Doljani and what you know of your own direct knowledge about them. And please do not take too much time in answering, because we don't have much time. So very briefly, please, will you tell this Honourable Court the fate of civilians in Konjic in the Nerevtica Valley, I mean Croat civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of this scenario which is in the document that I have in front of me, the fate of civilians in the municipality of Konjic, in the area of Nerevtica is as a matter of fact dramatic, because dramatic things happened there with very tragic consequences for the civilians. Very serious murders start, incarceration, persecution, destruction of property, arson. And this cannot be justified by any military necessity. In several places, in about 17 places in -- in about 17 places, Croats are detained. There is large-scale persecution of civilians. Over 90 per cent of them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I must object again because the Defence counsel is going on with the same line of questioning that just was discussed before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, we have discussed this matter already. I hope you could change the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really do not know where this leads to. It seems to me that I'm doing a futile job. The Prosecution, and they have the same kind of ethics as we do, they may not conceal matters, even though the indictment speaks to the contrary. All these are events which happened before the 15th of April, and if you could only hear what happened after the 15th of April? But I'll change the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: One cannot escape the truth. There is always time for the truth. Tell me, Jablanica, you were in Jablanica. What goes on in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 15th of April onward, that is 16, 17th, doesn't matter. So up to April and from April on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Right. So in Jablanica, in the territory of the municipality of Jablanica, in the area of Doljani, members of the BH Army launch attacks on the HVO, and it is precisely on the 15th of April that a large number or almost all Muslim civilians from the village -- in the village of Doljani move from Doljani to Jablanica. That day, in the town of Jablanica, the museum camp is formed. That same day, the first group of six Croats was taken to that camp. And members of the civilian police search --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Excuse me, but maybe the witness will specify the source of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness said he was there. Am I right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I was there, and I saw, and I'm speaking about what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I saw how Muslim civilians from the village of Doljani came. I know that that day, the 15th of April, the first group of six Croats was taken to the museum. I saw how my parents house was searched. I was there. And I was warned not to go away because I should go to my flat, so that my flat could be searched and I did that. I also know that that and the next day, all Croat flats in Jablanica were searched. I also know that almost all vehicles, cars, belonging to Croats were seized, were taken. The same thing befell our priest there, Alojzije Bosnjak, and I'm telling you only about what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, when did the incarceration of Croats began in the camp in Jablanica? And where was this camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The camp in Jablanica was housed in the former museum of the revolution, which is in the centre of the town. The first group, the six of them, were put there on the 15th, and their number grew so that towards the end of 1993, there were about 450 Croats in that camp. Those are people from Jablanica, those are civilians from Doljani, whom the members of the BH Army captured when they attacked Doljani on the 28th of July, 1993. They are civilian survivors from Grabovica, which is a municipality adjacent to Mostar - 90 of them. Who after the horrific murder of 33 civilians in that village, that is the survivors were brought there. And there also accidental passers-by who were Croats. Croats from the municipality of Konjic, people who were evicted from their flats in Jablanica and neighbouring municipalities. So that is the museum camp in Jablanica. Another camp was in Ostrozac, again in the municipality of Jablanica. And they were civilians from the Croat -- from Croat civilians from the village of Radosine. Some 85 of them. And then the third camp is Zukina Baza in Donja -- lower Jablanica. And it was established somewhat later. And I was in that camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there is any dispute about those camps. During the war, both sides, I must say, established certain camps and terrible things happened in those camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any women and children in those camps throughout?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We are on the same track, it seems to me, tu quoque defence. We cannot get rid of it today. Now we are talking about camps created in July, 1993. It could be explicable when we talk about April 1993 but not July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it seems to me that we will get nowhere if we are going along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I agree, and I'm really afraid that we shall get nowhere. But if I'm not allowed to challenge and refute the allegations in the indictment, then I certainly will not get anywhere. Secondly, my defence is not tu quoque and this is not the tu quoque defence. It is the refutation of the count in the indictment that the Croats persecuted people in the town of Jablanica and on the 16th of April, 1993, they started widespread persecution and ethnic cleansing. I called witnesses to refute those counts in the indictment. I do not go into specific crimes, nor am I trying to justify crime by another crime. This witness here is telling us that up to 15th of April, civilians were detained in camps, that is Croat civilians, that they were persecuted and ethnically cleansed from those areas. This is an eyewitness to these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have no doubt about that. We have no doubt at all about that. And you have the right, full right, to attack the indictment. But in another way. As I said before, during the wars, terrible things were committed by both sides. We have no doubts about that but the problem is that to put a very valid defence on your case. If you said that the HVO did not commit any atrocities, you may say that. But it is not right to blame the other parties that they had already committed certain crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, no, no, Your Honours. Then obviously we are talking at cross-purposes. Perhaps it is my fault and perhaps I haven't explained it properly. No, that is not it. I'm not trying to put the blame on somebody else and there seek the justification for some other forms of conduct, no, no. I am merely establishing the fact that what the indictment says, two counts in the indictment that I'm attacking, with witnesses who are here, I wish to refute those two counts, and those are Jablanica and widespread persecution, that is cleansing, started by the HVO. That is why I called this witness. And I'm simply asking him what happened in Jablanica. Did the HVO really do that? And the witness is answering and as soon as he starts to answer he's not allowed to continue because tu quoque then is brought up. It has nothing to do with tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is not important for the issue that who started the ethnic cleansing. The problem is that, whether HVO committed the ethnic cleansing in that area. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You heard the question. Tell us, let's do it that way. Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: That is nonsense. The HVO did not commit ethnic cleansing. Your Honours, don't forget, don't disregard the fact about the demographic and ethnic facts in the territory of the municipality of Jablanica that I told you about in 1992 and 1993. That is in the territory of the municipality of Jablanica, at that critical point in time, there were about 30.000 Muslims, of whom a large number are able-bodied men. The HVO is a negligible military force when compared with the BH Army forces. That is all that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Namely, can you explain what really happened in Jablanica, in the municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Since the ratio of those armed forces, as I have already said, in the territory of Jablanica, or more exactly in the village of Doljani, were members of the BH Army start an attack on the HVO in the area of Doljani. And then later on, it spreads also to the area of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, let me ask a specific question and then we'll move on to specific documents to round off this subject. It is also alleged that the HVO attacked Sovici and Doljani so as to engage in persecution. What do you personally know about those events? I mean the 15th, 16th, 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I know that the members of the BH Army attacked the HVO on the 15th of April in the area of Doljani, and on the 17th of April, since before that the HVO, because of the relief and because of the positions, it was always encircled by the BH Army, so the BH Army attacked the HVO in the area of Sovici on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge how many members of the HVO there were in Doljani and Jablanica on the 17th of April? And where do you have that knowledge from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I was not a soldier, because I was not able-bodied, but my brother was, for a while, the commander of an HVO battalion. It is through him --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where was he the commander of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: He was in -- a commander in Doljani in 1992. And this date that you're asking me about, at that time, not a single member of the HVO was in the town of Jablanica, and even long before that date that you are asking me about, there were no HVO members in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there in Jablanica and did they provide shifts for Sovici and Doljani and how far are those two places, Sovici and Doljani, how far are those places from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: You are not clear whose soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Soldiers from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In the territory of Sovici Doljani, that is Sovici, there was the Independent Battalion, over 250 strong, members of the 44 Mountain Brigade from Jablanica provided shifts for them or rather they provided them with the overall logistics, that is they went from Jablanica to the areas of Doljani and Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What do you personally know about the civilian population in Sovici, of Muslim origin? Do you know their lot? Do you know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. After the conflict in Sovici, Muslim civilians were evacuated from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where did they go? Was there some exchange with Croat civilians? Where did you go? Do you know anything about that? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes. They came to Jablanica in early June, 1993, after an exchange for Croat civilians from the village of Radosine. That village was attacked by the BH Army members and members of the HVO went to the camp at Celibici and the civilians from Radosine were at Ostrozac and then they were exchanged for the civilians from Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know where did the Croats go and where did the Muslim civilians from Sovici go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Croats went to Celibici, which is a village in the Konjic municipality. And then through the northern area towards Nevesinje and eventually to Mostar. And Muslim civilians come to Jablanica and force their way into Croat flats and apartments and houses in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the Croats from those houses and flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Croat civilians from the town, from those houses and flats, well, some of them find accommodation with their friends and some end up in the museum camp in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my final question on that subject, and then we shall move on to documents, how long did you spend in a camp, where and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: I spent six months in a camp. First at the Zukina Baza in Donja Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who is"Zuka"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Zulfikar Halispago,"Zuka", commander of the special purposes units attached to the staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina so a special unit in Jablanica and that is where we were brought. After two months, we were taken to the parish church in Dreznica which is the municipality of Mostar, and after 29 days we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Wait. The camp was in a church?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In the church, in the church. 29 days later we went back to the base of Zuka's troops, and finally on the 4th of November, that is on the 4th of November, 1993, we were taken to the museum camp in Jablanica and I was there until the truce on the 31st of March -- no, sorry, 1st of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time that the HVO also ran some camps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, I was. In mid-September, 1993, in the -- in the Zuka's base, in the camp there, some Muslim detainees came who had been to Dretelj in Capljina. They came there to guard us. They were our guards. And they also ill-treated us, harassed us by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I do not want to ask you about anything you went through in those camps. I want to spare you and I want to save some time. So let us move on to documents. And my first question is: Did you, and when, actively cooperate with the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I cooperated with The Hague investigators between April, 1995 and intensively until the end of 1996. And then, now and then, for a part of 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many documents or videotapes did you hand over to The Hague investigators in 1995? You personally, I mean. And who was it that you gave them to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: It was like this. In April 1995, we handed over a small number of documents, about 250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think that the Defence counsel should explain what is the relevance, of a different case to this case, and participation of this witness in some different investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, lay some foundations for us, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To begin with, I don't know what investigation the Prosecutor is referring to, because had we allowed the witness to tell us to the end, it wasn't only one specific investigation, and it is precisely what I said the other day, Your Honours, but I will not testify. The witness will testify. He turned over several thousand documents which The Hague Tribunal has. You will hear the name of the man that the witness gave these documents to. Documents and videotapes. And which are exculpatory for this part of the indictment we are talking about, my client. Why don't you hear a little bit about how the investigation was conducted between 1995 and 2002. The gentleman was with them on the ground actively every day. And you can hear many interesting things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you're being too general. Can you ask specific questions? Did he cooperate with The Hague left in the air? [as interpreted] Did you give any documents left in the air? You have to direct the questions. Ask specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This was my intention but the Prosecutor interrupted my first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was it who you cooperated with among the investigators of the Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In April, 1995, Mr. Tom Kampanos [phoen], a representative of the office of the Hague Tribunal in Zagreb, arrived in Mostar and announced the arrival of a team of investigators from The Hague Tribunal, whose Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. objective was to investigate war crimes against civilians and prisoners of war in the Operation Neretva, 1993. That was the operation conducted by the Army of BH in the territory of the municipalities of Prozor, Konjic and Mostar. At that time, he was handed over about 250 documents which indicate that a crime was committed against civilians in Konjic municipality, in Orliste village. In that same year, on the 31st of August, I personally, in the offers of the Hague Tribunal in Zagreb, handed over over 3.700 written documents and some videotapes about the crimes committed in the area that I have just mentioned. The investigation during 1995 and 1996, that is to say the team of investigators, was led by Mr. Jis Avivad [phoen]. At the end of the investigation, he thanked me for good cooperation, and he announced that charges would be raised against 13 persons, Muslims, members of the BH Army. Those were persons ranking from very low positions, such as a guard in a detention camp, to the highest posts of generals, commanders, high -- top officers of the BH Army. The -- he announced that charges would be raised in 1977, as soon as the elections were over and the elections that I'm referring to were the ones scheduled --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: 1997 was the year, so immediately after the elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, at the beginning of 1997, a new investigation team of the Hague Tribunal came, led by Mr. Nikolai Mihajov [phoen] and they tried to -- they tried to put in a different light everything that the previous team had done before, put in a very relative light. And we were suggested that the people in this new team were not well-meaning, that their goal was to see this investigation come to nothing, as a matter of fact. Unfortunately, it seems to me personally that this was really true, because after seven years, that lapsed from the end of this investigation, I have not heard of any indictment, although in this area that was the subject of this investigation, several hundred civilians were killed, 25.000 civilians were expelled, 25 camps were organised, where several -- that several dozens of Croatian inmates were either killed or perished, and they were all victims of the inhumane and cruel treatment in these camps. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Has anybody asked you to testify personally before this Tribunal, before me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I still have five minutes left for the documents. So I would kindly ask Madam Registrar to help me. I would like to put all the documents in front of the witness that is D1333, D1334, D1335, D1336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341. My first question, starting with the document 333, the first question is: Have you given me all these documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have you given the same documents in 1995 to the Prosecutor of the Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The first document, 333, just one sentence: What is this document? What does it represent? It speaks very much for itself. We don't have to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What we really want to know is where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard the question. Can we have the answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document comes from the Commission for the Establishment of War Crimes, and some documents I -- about the war events,

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So can you give -- can you tell the Honourable Judge Clark the provenance of these documents? How you came by them and where from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Since I was an active actor of this commission, of this centre, I had the opportunity to see all these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who gave them to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The documents came from the following sources. From the military prosecutor, from the military court, from certain witnesses who -- potential witnesses, who came for interviews with the investigators of the Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In one sentence, what is this Exhibit 333?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: This document, as a matter of fact, is the document which paves the way politically, for the implementation of the Operation Neretva 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's move on to document 334.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: 334 is a certificate of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Don't say anything mentioning your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: This is my personal certificate certifying to the fact that I was registered in the museum camp in Jablanica between these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's move on to 335.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: These are two documents under one number. The first document on the top of the page confirms that I was called to take part in forced labour, although I was at the time of ill health, and I have the decision to that effect from the medical board. I still had to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the Defence counsel to explain the relevance of these documents, of this particular document, to our case at hand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, if you object to the admission of those documents, you may file your motions in seven days after the Defence counsel tenders those documents into evidence. Then the Court will make the proper decisions. Yes. You may go on, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: A few sentences about this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: So this document illustrates the fate of the Croats who found themselves in Jablanica in 1993. Although I was not an able-bodied person, I still had to work hard, but I was not an exception. Others had to do that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 336, we have already discussed. Let's move on to the -- no, let's skip D1334 because we have already discussed that document with some previous witnesses. We have now arrived at document 337.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: 337 confirms that Mr. Cibo, besides being an illegal president of the War Presidency, also, by way of this document, incorporated himself politically in Mostar, because it says here that he -- there will be more use for him in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: That's Mr. Omer Behmen, one of the top figures of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We move on to 338.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Document 338 indicates that there were preparations for the military implementation of the Operation Neretva 1993, so the deployment of troops, military technique and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But the date is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: 28th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did the preparations start as early as that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Document 339.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The same person, Mr. Cibo, who incorporated himself politically, now he is being deployed as a military person in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Corps in the Konjic-Mostar area, in order to be able to carry out the expected tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So Konjic, Prozor, Jablanica, this is the zone of responsibility of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The seat of the 4th Corps, where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The seat of the 4th Corps was in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: The commander was Arif Pasalic, General Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Move on to 340.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Document 340 confirms that in the municipality -- in Zlatar in Konjic municipality, a segment of the overall plan Neretva 1993 is being realised. So the HVO positions are attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So this is the same Zlatar from the previous document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The last document, 341?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Document 341 confirms the attempt on the part of the legally appointed president of the War Presidency in Konjic municipality to dispute the illegal appointment of Dr. Cibo was the president of the War Presidency so this was raised before the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina to dispute this act. However, this court never took this act into consideration because the then leadership, headed by Izetbegovic, did not show any will to discuss this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who filed the motion for the evaluation of constitutionality of this document on the replacement of the previous president and the appointment of the new president? Who is the one who filed that motion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: This was filed by Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic, the legally elected president of the War Presidency of Konjic municipality, on behalf of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This document speaks for itself so I won't go any further, witness. With the kindness of this Court, I have been able to go on even longer than I had intended to. Thank you very much for coming to testify here. Thank you for helping this Court. And with this, I would finish my direct examination, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any direct examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like first of all to distribute the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to remind you, Mr. Prosecutor, you also have 90 minutes to conducts the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How much time do I have before the break? I'm sorry, I'm a little bit confused now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's break at 5.30, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, first of all I would ask you to go into private session for some minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then maybe you will explain what were the functions of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: As the executive -- executive body of the local government under wartime conditions, its primary task was to ensure, to organise life, to provide for the organisation of life so as to meet the citizens' needs in those conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear reports from the chief of military police, of civilian police, on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I mean 1992 and 1992 when you were in that position. I mean April and November, according to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there until November. I didn't say I was there until November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. You told us that October.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now I wait for a response to my question. Did you receive daily reports from military police commander and civilian police commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: Yes, from the civilian police. No, from the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports from HVO command and, let's say, MOS command? Or Territorial Defence, as you called it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: We heard -- we received reports from the HVO command, but I know of, no, TO. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. I will call it in a different way. MOS, Muslim armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NE
utterances.text: In that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But now I see that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 6.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, could we have the witness, please? Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness comes back, I'd like to state the position of Mr. Martinovic's Defence in relation to documents and sources of documents, that is the point that was raised by Mr. Krsnik. Mr. Vinko Martinovic's Defence joins -- Mr. Vinko Martinovic's Defence joins the objections regarding the authenticity of these documents. We believe that one cannot say that these documents come from the BH government, because that means that the Prosecutor is authenticating those documents. In other words, it is not that we have a witness here who would be telling us now that these documents are in the hands of the BH government and so on and so forth. The very concept, the source, is the BH government, it simply does not mean anything to us. If we could hear this is in the government's archive, it is perhaps in some other national archives, that would be another matter. When the Prosecutor, during the presentation of his case, when he produced documents, he brought -- he called witnesses, fact witnesses, and it was never said the sources the government of Croatia, the government of the Republic of Croatia. The Prosecutor brought their investigators and then they said, "Well, I spoke to the government of the Republic of Croatia. I went to the archive and obtained -- and found there this and that. So this is the gist of our objection.
